summary: The evaluator, the contract and a recorded starting board are in place, and the judge runs on every submission. Rows may be re-validated before the challenge goes live.

gates.name: Trusted evaluator with tests that require it to refuse seeded defects
gates.evidence: challenges/binohash/evaluator, challenges/binohash/tests/test_evaluator.py: fourteen defects, each refused at its stage

gates.name: Reference engine agrees with Bitcoin Core's consensus library on pinned spends
Starting board measured on public lanes with the Core comparison
Parameter search run against the security and work models before opening
gates.evidence: challenges/binohash/README.md (what the first search found): four corrections to the judge from a parameter search and three from an agent search against the first board, each with a regression test; the board was re-recorded under BH-SEC-2 with six instances

gates.name: Starting board validated by the judge pipeline with ledger-key seeds
gates.evidence: challenges/binohash/results.tsv (kind = historical): six instances validated at the full stage with ledger-key seeds and the Core comparison; the rows were assembled on a maintainer's machine, not by the hosted judge

gates.name: Judge workflow: sandboxed build, trusted evaluation, signed ledger rows
gates.evidence: .github/workflows/judge.yml, spec/VALIDATION.md; exercised locally end to end; the harness workflow passes on hosted runners; the judge itself has not yet run on a pull request

gates.name: First submission judged end to end on hosted runners
Independent review of the security model BH-SEC-2
A production-difficulty spend of the standard baseline accepted by Bitcoin Core
Written and reviewed soundness argument for the final candidate of each track
